title: LOCATE: Learning-Based Localization of Obfuscated FSM State Registers via Timing and Switching-Activity Fingerprints
content: Finite-state machines (FSMs) are widely used to implement control logic in digital systems and are therefore important targets for intellectual property protection and hard ware obfuscation. Although FSM obfuscation aims to conceal the underlying control behavior, its implementation may leave measurable characteristics that distinguish obfuscated FSM (OFSM) state registers from other sequential elements. This work investigates whether OFSM state registers protected us ing the ProtectIP state-space obfuscation methodology can be localized using only timing and switching-activity information, without relying on register names or explicit structural features. Specifically, setup timing, hold timing, and switching activity are used to construct a numerical profile for each flip-flop. LOCATE is evaluated across six benchmark designs containing 4,743 flip flops, including 331 OFSM state registers. Under within-design five-fold validation, the approach identifies 281 of the 331 OFSM registers with only 14 false positives, achieving 95.3% precision, 84.9% recall, and an F1 score of 89.8%. More importantly, leave-one-design-out cross-design evaluation, in which the target circuit is completely excluded from training, achieves 87.2% precision, 80.4% recall, and an F1 score of 83.6%. Feature ablation analysis further shows that setup and hold timing provide the strongest discrimination, while switching activity contributes complementary information that improves overall localization performance. These results demonstrate that FSM obfuscation can leave transferable implementation-level finger prints and highlight timing and switching activity as potential sources of information leakage for localizing protected state registers in previously unseen obfuscated designs.
